edges.description: Bmpr1b-null mice show reduced proliferation in the phalangeal region after normal initial digital-ray formation. This provides model-based support for a developmental consequence of impaired receptor signaling.
Loss of Bmpr1b reduces phalangeal chondrocyte differentiation in mice; the human developmental mechanism is inferred from this perturbation model.
Reduced expansion of digital precursors is a model-supported contributor to distal skeletal underdevelopment; it does not by itself explain every human fusion or fibular defect.

Deficient digital chondrocyte differentiation offers a partial developmental explanation for the human distal-limb malformations. Precise routes to individual skeletal abnormalities remain unresolved.
